# Filtering and Checking P-element, Shellder and Spoink insertions into piRNA clusters

Insertions were identified with sniffles2 and intersected with piRNA clusters annotation.

Here, some filtering was applied below to eliminate insertions with low support (support \<2).

Moreover, insertions in piRNA clusters with less than 5 reads of support (total) or less than 3 reads spanning the insertions were flagged to be inspected in IGV.

Finally, some insertions were edited to include piRNA cluster information.

## 1. Load libraries

```{r message = FALSE}
library(readxl)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(writexl)
library(readr)
```

## 2. Load data

```{r}
#edited dataset of all insertions found using Sniflles2 crosmatched with the TE annotation from the assemled genomes and the piRNA cluster annotation
insertions<-read_excel("P_Shellder_Spoink_all_strains_insertions_ed.xlsx")
insertions<-insertions%>%
  mutate(SUP_SPAN=SUPPORT -  SUPPORT_LONG)

#piRNA cluster annotation to recover complete information
pics_info<-read.table("summary_piCs_after_liftover.tsv", header=TRUE)
```

```{r}
pics_info_selected<-pics_info%>%
  select(Chrom_R,Start_RF,End_RF,piC_number, Strain, unique_sample_count)
write_tsv(pics_info_selected, "pics_info_selected.bed", col_names = FALSE)
```

## 3. Filtering: support \>=2

Eliminating insertions with only 1 support read.

```{r}
insertions_filtered1 <- insertions %>%
  filter(SUPPORT>=2)
```

## 4. Creating insertion index

```{r}
insertions_filtered1 <- insertions_filtered1 %>%
  arrange(CHROM, POS) %>%
  group_by(CHROM, POS) %>%
  mutate(insertion = if_else(
    is.na(CHROM) | is.na(POS),
    NA_integer_,
    cur_group_id()
  )) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## 5. Strains

```{r}
all = c("Cro18","AA1","AA12","AH24","AH33","AH35","Hin17","Lps3","Lps5","LSD01","LSD07","MD221","MD233","MSC01","MSC04","PUS102","PUS412","SGA12","SGA20","SGA26","SGA27","SGA34")
pstrains = c("Cro18","AH24","AH33","AH35","LSD01","LSD07","MSC01","MSC04","PUS102","PUS412")
mstrains  = setdiff(all, pstrains)
```

## 6. Insertions in piCs

```{r}
insertions_pics<-insertions_filtered1%>%
  filter(pic!="no")
```

### 6.1 piCs containing P element

```{r}
P_ins<-insertions_filtered1%>%
  filter(TE=="P_Ds#DNA/P")
P_ins_pic<-insertions_pics%>%
  filter(TE=="P_Ds#DNA/P")
P_ins_pic_check<-P_ins_pic%>%
  filter(SUPPORT<=5|SUP_SPAN<=3)
```

#### 6.1.1 Visual Inspection

Three insertions were removed after IGV inspection (LSD07: 2, 3; MSC04: 230); MSC04 insertion 1 was retained.

```{r}
P_ins_pics_filtered <- P_ins_pic %>%
  filter(!(Strain == "LSD07" & insertion %in% c(2, 3))) %>%
  filter(!(Strain == "MSC04" & insertion == "230")) 
```

#### 6.1.2 Adding additional piCs

This insertion was clearly found in IGV, but it was not called in Sniffles2 (AH33: 1).

```{r}
new_row <- tibble::tibble(
  Strain = "AH33",              
  Status_copy = "Non-assembled",         
  TEbed_chrom = "NC_052520.2_RagTag",
  TEbed_start1 = 56284,
  TEbed_end1 = NA,
  TEbed_strand = NA,
  pic = "1",
  CHROM = "NC_052520.2",
  POS = 73341,
  ID = "Sniffles2.INS.46S0",
  SVLEN = 5819,
  SUPPORT = 52,
  SUPPORT_LONG = 30,
  AF = 1.000,
  GT = "1/1",
  GQ = 60,
  DR = 0,
  DV = 199,
  TE = "P_Ds#DNA/P",
  TSD = "AGGCAGAG(nested GGACCACC)",
  LiftChrom = NA,
  LiftStart0 = NA,
  LiftEnd0 = NA,
  SUP_SPAN = 22,
  insertion = 2
)

P_ins_pics_filtered_add1 <- bind_rows(P_ins_pics_filtered, new_row)
```

Coordinates of P insertions in the reference genome were intersected with the trasffered piC coordinates across all strains. Although the initial analysis considered only piCs predicted within each strain, this extended comparison was performed to identify regions that may not have been called as piCs in a given strain due to filtering or parameter settings. Candidate regions were then visually inspected in IGV to confirm whether they display a piRNA distribution consistent with bona fide piRNA clusters. The insertions should have good support as well.

One extra insertion in piC should be considered. (MSC01: insertion 821; NC_052525.2:82144) - It corresponds to the cluster 677 - piRNA cluster predicted in 8 strains.

```{r}
P_MSC01_677<- P_ins %>%
  filter(Strain == "MSC01" & insertion == 821) %>%
  mutate(pic = 677)%>%
  mutate(pic = as.character(pic))
P_ins_pics_filtered_add2 <- bind_rows(P_ins_pics_filtered_add1, P_MSC01_677)
```

#### 6.1.3 Join tables

```{r warning = FALSE}
P_ins_pics_filtered_add2$pic<-as.character(P_ins_pics_filtered_add2$pic)

pics_info$piC_number<-as.character(pics_info$piC_number)

P_ins_pics_filtered_info <- left_join(
  P_ins_pics_filtered_add2,
  pics_info,
  by = c("pic" = "piC_number", "Strain" = "Strain")
)

#mannually adding the information about the new piC
P_ins_pics_filtered_info <-P_ins_pics_filtered_info%>%
  mutate(
    unique_sample_count= ifelse (Strain=="MSC01" & insertion == 821,8,unique_sample_count),
Status= ifelse (Strain=="MSC01" & insertion == 821, "Shared", Status)
  )
#The join step can increase the number of records because fragmented piRNA cluster annotations in some strains produce redundant matches for the same insertion. To resolve redundant entries, records were grouped by `Strain`, `insertion`, and `pic`. For each group, the entry was prioritized if the insertion coordinate (`TEbed_start`) fell within the cluster interval (`Start_S`–`End_S`). When no matching interval was found, a single representative entry was retained.

P_clean <- P_ins_pics_filtered_info %>%
  group_by(Strain, insertion, pic) %>%
  mutate(
    inside_interval = case_when(
      !is.na(TEbed_start1) & !is.na(Start_S) & !is.na(End_S) &
        TEbed_start1 >= Start_S & TEbed_start1 <= End_S ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(inside_interval), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-inside_interval)

P_save<-P_clean%>%
  select("Strain", "Status_copy", "TEbed_chrom","TEbed_start1","TEbed_end1",          "CHROM", "POS", "ID","SVLEN", "SUPPORT", "SUPPORT_LONG" , "TSD", "LiftChrom", "LiftStart0", "insertion", "pic","Chrom_R","Start_R","End_R","Chrom_S", "Start_S" , "End_S", "program",  "unique_sample_count" ,"Status", "Strains")

colnames(P_save)<-c("Strain", "Status_copy", "TE_chrom","TE_start","TE_end", "Sniffles_INS_CHROM", "Sniffles_INS_TE_POS", "Sniffles_INS_ID","Sniffles_INS_SVLEN", "Sniffles_INS_SUPPORT", "Sniffles_INS_SUPPORT_LONG" , "TSD", "INS_LiftChrom", "INS_LiftStart", "insertion","piC_number", "piC_Chrom_Ref","piC_Start_Ref","piC_End_Ref", "piC_Chrom_Strain", "Start_Strain" , "End_Strain", "program",  "piC_strain_count" ,"Status_piC", "Strains_sharing_piC")
```

#### 6.1.4 Saving P table

```{r}
write_tsv (P_save,"piCs_containing_P_insertions.tsv")
```

### 6.2 piCs containing Shellder

```{r}
Shellder_ins<-insertions_filtered1%>%
  filter(TE=="Shellder_Ds#LTR/Gypsy")
#pics with sniffles confirmation
Shellder_ins_pic<-insertions_pics%>%
  filter(TE=="Shellder_Ds#LTR/Gypsy")
Shellder_ins_pic_check<-Shellder_ins_pic%>%
  filter(SUPPORT<=5|SUP_SPAN<=3)
```

#### 6.2.1 Adding additional piCs

Coordinates of Sheldler insertions in the reference genome were intersected with the transferred piC coordinates across all strains. Although the initial analysis considered only piCs predicted within each strain, this extended comparison was performed to identify regions that may not have been called as piCs in a given strain due to filtering or parameter settings. Candidate regions were then visually inspected in IGV to confirm whether they display a piRNA distribution consistent with bona fide piRNA clusters. The insertions should have good support as well. In some cases, the insertions were predicted in a region of the reference that was not lifted to the original strain; thus, intersecting the reference coordinates is essential to identity the insertions (although it is not possible to check them in IGV).

9 insertions should be considered:

SGA12: insertion 192 - NC_052520.2:22425792; Non-lifted insertion; pic 197 present in 22 strains

SGA26 insertion 198 - NC_052520.2:22768535;Non-lifted insertion; pic 203 present in 22 strains

LSD07 insertion 217 - NC_052521.2 2082214; predicted pic coordinates in LSD07 is shorter not including the region of the insertion, but it should be extended; pic 241 present in 22 strains

SGA26 insertion 1010 - NC_052525.2:21124740- Non-lifted insertion; flam1

Lps3 insertion 1016 - NC_052525.2:21278474; predicted pic is shorter; flam1

PUS102 insertion 1070 - NW_025416856.1:380584; Non-lifted insertion; flam2

PUS102 insertion 1072 - NW_025416856.1:412944 412945; Non-lifted insertion; flam2

SGA27 insertion 1081 - NW_025416877.1 656656; Non-lifted insertion; pic 904 present in 10 strains

AA1 - assembled insertion NW_025416856.1_RagTag:185599-192265 not recovered by sniffles - but the region is correct in IGV. Potentially the insertion region is missing in the reference as it is a TE-rich region - pic 870

```{r}
Shellder_ins_ed <- Shellder_ins %>%
  mutate(
    pic = case_when(
      Strain == "SGA12"  & insertion == 192  ~ "197",
      Strain == "SGA26"  & insertion == 198  ~ "203",
      Strain == "LSD07"  & insertion == 217  ~ "241",
      Strain == "SGA27"  & insertion == 1081  ~ "904",
      Strain == "SGA26"  & insertion == 1010 ~ "flam1",
      Strain == "Lps3"   & insertion == 1016 ~ "flam1",
      Strain == "PUS102" & insertion == 1070 ~ "flam2",
      Strain == "PUS102" & insertion == 1072 ~ "flam2",
      TRUE ~ as.character(pic)
    )
  )

Shellder_AA1<- insertions %>%
  filter(Strain == "AA1" & pic == 870)

Shellder_ins_ed_add_pics <- bind_rows(Shellder_ins_ed, Shellder_AA1)%>%
  filter(pic!="no")
```

#### 6.2.2 Visual inspection

Seven insertions were removed after IGV inspection (MSC01:190; Lps5:173, 208; MD221: 383, 561 , 919; PUS102: 1097).

```{r}
#MSC01 - insertion 190
#Lps5 insertion173 and 208
#MD221 -insertion 383, 561 , 919
#PUS102 insertion 1097
Shellder_ins_pics_filtered<-Shellder_ins_ed_add_pics %>%
  filter(!(Strain == "MSC01" & insertion == "190"))%>%
      filter(!(Strain == "Lps5" & insertion %in% c(173, 208)))%>%
         filter(!(Strain == "MD221" & insertion %in% c(383, 561,919)))%>%
            filter(!(Strain == "PUS102" & insertion == "1097"))
```

#### 6.2.4 Editing flamenco clusters

Flamenco 1 and 2 are broken in our results due to the presence of genes internally. We edited the dataset, so they are not considered independent clusters.

**Flamenco 1 - coordinates in the REF genome:** NC_052525.2:21072908-21518427

From Dsim flamenco promoter NC_052525.2:21072908-21072947 to first Dip1 gene downstream flamenco NC_052525.2:21518427-21517464. It encompasses 2 clusters in our dataset:

**pic 813:** NC_052525.2:21071002-21200919

gene: TcTp gene interrupts flamenco 1 in some strains. It seems to have been inserted by retroposition.

**pic 814:** NC_052525.2:21201858-21517404

**Flamenco 2 -** **coordinates in the REF genome:** NW_025416856.1:19298-598917

The 3' limit of flamenco 2 is harder to establish. We considered the last cluster without interruption of functional genes upstream su(f) suppressor of forked gene. 5' limit is the flamenco promoter. It encompasses at least 3 clusters in our dataset:

**pic 870**: NW_025416856.1: 17436-304993

**gene**: uncharacterized protein LOC6740449

**pic 871:** NW_025416856.1:307843-333001

**gene**: LOC27208153; pseudogene

**pic 872**: NW_025416856.1: 336172-442148

**PROBABLY THE LIMIT OF FLAMENCO2 IS HERE**

**gene**: LOC6740432; antigen 5 like allergen Cul n 1

**pic 873** NW_025416856.1: 443983-503477

**gene**: LOC120285602; FACT

**pic 874:** NW_025416856.1: 503832-504847

```{r}
Shellder_clean_ed<-Shellder_clean%>%
  mutate(pic = case_when(
    pic %in% c(813,814) ~ "flam1", 
    pic %in% c(870, 871, 872) ~ "flam2",
    TRUE ~ as.character(pic)  ))
```
